Section 1.

Subd. 2a.
Health professional's medical statement.

The medical statement [-that the applicant is a physically disabled person-] must specify whether the disability is permanent or temporary and, if temporary, the opinion of the health professional as to the duration of the disability.

Sec. 3.

[+Subd. 6.+]

[+(1) an application in the form and manner acceptable to the commissioner; and +]

[+(i) the applicant has been diagnosed with cancer; +]

bill_text.plain_text:
A bill for an act relating to transportation; authorizing issuance of cancer-related disability parking certificates; amending Minnesota Statutes 2024, section 169.345, subdivisions 2a, 3b, by adding a subdivision.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF MINNESOTA:

Section 1.
Minnesota Statutes 2024, section 169.345, subdivision 2a, is amended to read:

Subd. 2a.
Health professional's medical statement.
(a) The commissioner must develop a format for the medical statement. The medical statement must be signed by a health professional who certifies that the applicant is (1) a physically disabled person as defined in subdivision 2, or (2) eligible for a certificate under subdivision 6. The commissioner may request additional information from the health professional if needed to verify the applicant's eligibility. The medical statement must specify whether the disability is permanent or temporary and, if temporary, the opinion of the health professional as to the duration of the disability.
(b) A health professional who fraudulently certifies to the commissioner that a person is eligible for the disability plates authorized by section 168.021 or a certificate authorized by this section, is guilty of a misdemeanor and is subject to a fine of $500.
(c) The commissioner may waive the requirement of providing a statement of a health professional if the applicant has previously filed with the commissioner a statement of a health professional certifying that the applicant has a permanent physical disability.

Sec. 2.
Minnesota Statutes 2024, section 169.345, subdivision 3b, is amended to read:

Subd. 3b.
Certificate design, format, information.
(a) A certificate must be made of plastic or similar durable material and must bear its expiration date prominently on both sides. A certificate issued on a temporary basis must display the date of expiration as determined under subdivision 3 , 3a, or 6.
(b) Each applicant must be provided a summary of the parking privileges and restrictions that apply to each motor vehicle for which the certificate is used.

Sec. 3.
Minnesota Statutes 2024, section 169.345, is amended by adding a subdivision to read:

Subd. 6.

Cancer-related certificate.

(a) The commissioner must issue a certificate under this section to an applicant who submits:

(1) an application in the form and manner acceptable to the commissioner; and

(2) a medical statement under subdivision 2a that affirms:

(i) the applicant has been diagnosed with cancer;

(ii) due to the diagnosis or an associated condition or treatment, the applicant is experiencing any of the conditions described in subdivision 2, paragraph (f); and

(iii) the circumstances in items (i) and (ii) are expected to apply for at least 30 days.

(b) A certificate issued under this subdivision is valid for up to 12 months.

(c) The operator of a vehicle displaying a certificate has the parking privileges provided in subdivision 1 only while the vehicle is actually parked while transporting a person for whom the certificate is issued.
